notes.title: Devlog on the upcoming free Chemistry Update
notes.notes:
[p][/p][p]Hello Everyone! We figured it was time to provide an update on the state of the game, as it’s become clearer and clearer the changes are big enough that they’re not just right around the corner. My name is Ryan; you might have seen me on the Discord or Steam boards helping people and answering questions. We are a [i]very[/i] small team and everyone does multiple jobs, but in the loosest possible terms, I program (almost) everything. I am responsible for the art direction (not specific assets) and many of the design decisions are mine (though we’re super collaborative on this and make a lot of team decisions). I joke that I am responsible for all the bugs because this is 100% true. I am the bottleneck on the next update and am definitely moments away from covering my office in red yarn. This update is a DOOZY. In this devlog, I’ll talk about what I’ve been up to and what’s left to do. At the end, we’ll talk a bit about DLC, free updates, and what to expect from us as we continue working on this game.[/p][p][/p][p][i]Ryan also recorded a separate video where he walks through the progress he's made in Unreal. You can check out that video here! But if you're interested in reading about the development process and everything that Ryan's had to do so far to make the chemistry update possible, and all the things he's had to take into consideration and the systems he's had to muck around with, read on![/i][/p][previewyoutube="44OASY0M0iA;full"][/previewyoutube][h2]
Chemistry[/h2][p]For better or worse, Fish Keeping is a lot of chemistry. I think most people aren’t drawn in to fish keeping for the test tubes and PPM readouts, but at the end of the day we love our fish which makes us become home chemists. The focus of Fish Game should be on the fish, so for the past 5 years our focus has been on that layer of the experience. I feared if we started with Chemistry we’d end up making Plumbing Simulator, and that’s just not what brings most people into the hobby. That said, we’re now at the stage in development where the only way forward is through the invisible connections happening in the water. This update is exciting, and interesting, and boring, and slow, and complicated, and super important.[/p][h2]
Research[/h2][p]Ok, let’s start with the complicated. It’s always tempting to overcomplicate, and game designing experience has taught me to resist overcomplication. However, one of the implicit promises in Fish Game is that if something is happening--it’s really happening. So for Chemistry, the [i]very[/i] specific relationships between each element must mimic the REAL thing. There is an equation for pH and many interlocking relationships between pH and everything else. There are interactions in the nitrogen cycle that make either the Walstad Method or High Tech setups viable. Temperature has a cascading effect into basically everything in an aquatic environment. The point is that this is not a recommended game development decision, but we’re doing very thorough research on the actual relationships between about 20 different chemical elements/constructs/systems. We’re looking for real data to make sure the system we’re making is spitting out reality at least in the big picture. Our sources (in order) are scientific papers, books, cited blog posts, actual measurements posted online, veteran experience, corroborated forum posts, mob vibes, and (if all else fails) personal experience. It is slow, difficult work with a lot of dead ends--but when all the equations are in place, the number ranges are confirmed with real world measurements, the time scales are normalized, and the connections between chemical concepts are hooked together--reality just falls out on the screen.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44655584/96a2193eb9085df156e47bbbe175617b65ac35f3.png"][/img][i]Some of the madness occupying my desk right now. My Chrome tabs make this look absolutely tidy.[/i][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44655584/07d7f7ddd069f06aaa22627b11a024c6ddec0c23.png"][/img][/p][p][i]A Google Sheets tool I made for finding the connections between chemistry parameters. You can read it like this-B16 (Algae) affects K16 (Ammonia) by lowering it. B9 (Food) does not affect H9 (Temp). This tool helps me not miss obvious connections I originally did not think to include.[/i][/p][p][/p][p]For example: I spent weeks on pH and CO2. They are tightly related because CO2 is one of the most present acids in a fish tank, and, frankly, we heavy planters are very focused on it. For days on end I worked to plug in tables of data from research papers, make PPMs match measurements taken from standard fish tanks, and match up formulas with the vibes on Reddit. It was complicated and boring and had no real interesting output. One day, I clicked one more Lego brick in place and, like [i]magic,[/i] the system came alive and started acting like the real thing. I noticed something unexpected when I raised the number of plants in the tank, so I searched online, “Can too many plants raise pH?” And of course they can, it turns out. So when everything is in place, the model has predictive power for real world chemistry that emerges from the system all on its own. That’s what we’re going for--we don’t describe every situation ahead of time. We give the game the rules of reality and reality describes itself.[/p][p][/p][h2][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44655584/9c409ba5d2a81fa7a72c936c0ebc7087d25257b4.png"][/img][/h2][h2]Graphs[/h2][p]But really who cares if no one can see what’s going on? The other half of getting chemistry right is getting player communication right. As I go, I have been making tools to surface the numbers in a more visual way for both myself and future players. We have a graph to show the long term relationships between factors and the effect of time. We have filters and groupings like “Nitrogen Cycle”, “Illness”, or “Beginner” to make it easier to see just a few related things at once. We have range suggestions to show the consequences of any stat going too high or too low. Just like Fish Stats, every Chemistry Stat has tooltips that show what has affected it and by how much. In its current state, the graph is ugly and practical (it will get a polish pass later), but already, it has made the chemistry much less abstract and more tangible and understandable. Whenever I reach a dead end, usually the solution is found in making the graphs more usable.[/p][p]My measure for success on this feature is that a complete fish keeping novice will wander in from Steam, fall in love with their goldfish Henry, discover that chemistry is important to keep Henry happy, slowly get introduced to the concepts in a way that’s not overwhelming, and, before they know it, they have intermediate to advanced knowledge of real world water chemistry. They’ll use it to keep the digital tank happy in the same way they would for a real tank, and if they ever dipped into the real thing, they would succeed with minimal effort. For those that are just not here for that level of commitment--I see you, and we will have robust settings to choose your level of engagement.[/p][h2]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44655584/ad26aace2c3d64c1bf0d3aa4a8163ca40864b600.png"][/img][/h2][h2]Equipment[/h2][p]On that note, let’s take a look at Equipment. For a few months now, the highest concern voiced by players is feeling like the game is too frantic. They want to design cool tanks, but they aren’t able to focus on that for long without their current tanks spinning out and turning into boxes of death. We do want a Creative Mode, but before doing that, I think it’s important for the game part of the game to feel balanced. The solution here is obviously Filters, Air Stones, Auto Feeders, etc. There are a million reasons why they aren’t in the game yet, but we’re working on them now because they are the other half of the Chemistry coin. Equipment will do two things--it gives players a way to play with the abstract concepts of Chemistry, but it also allows a certain level of automation that should give players a little more peace of mind when going to start another tank. Once that is in and working smoothly, of course we’ll make a Creative Mode.[/p][p]We’ve started poking at the equipment features, but first, the chemistry system needs to be designed in a way to pull in equipment as a means to play and interact with the game. There are a lot of unsolved problems about the game part of making aquarium equipment, and honestly, I’ve had a cloud of question marks hanging around the whole concept for several years now. We have the direction to head forward, but it’s still a bit hazy.[/p][h2]
Movement Tools Update[/h2][p]Along with an equipment feature set will come an upgrade to the movement tools. I love many things about the one we have for grabbing and moving hardscape, plants, and fish, but it has obvious limitations that I have meant to resolve for a long time now. Since aquarium equipment tends to be much more particular about [i]where[/i] it goes, I figured now was the best time to revisit this toolset and give it the upgrade it deserves. I have a plan, but there isn’t much to show yet.[/p][h2]
New Systems[/h2][p]Now with chemistry comes a lot of exciting new features that really only made sense to make after building the chemistry structure they would inhabit. We have Tannins that can leach into the water from botanicals or hardscape. We’re modeling botanicals like Catappa Leaves, and players will be able to scape with them. There is almost no research on this but enough fishkeeper experience to justify connecting Tannins to things like pH, bacterial growth, injury recovery, and fish stress. Soon I will be adding Flow, which, like temperature, acts as a connector for a large number of other Chemistry Stats. It will push things around in the tank, and I am looking into certain fish and plants either liking or disliking this happening. Equipment will have flow as a result either by accident or as the main feature. Bacteria will be joining the game, since it is such an important part of the nitrogen cycle. Bacteria are their own living system contained inside a few floating point number variables, but so far they are already showing the ability to bloom, crash, respond to the level of nutrition available, and die under extreme conditions. Yet another example of the real world playing out on the screen. [/p][h2]
DLC[/h2][p]Let’s talk about time. All of this work is slow, complex, and [i]not[/i] a fancy videogame marketing beat. We believe the art and craft of making an honest fish keeping simulator deserves this level of care. We have a vague timeline and expect the Chemistry Update won’t be ready for players until late Fall 2025. Every day spent working on this free update costs money, and the base game sales do not make enough to cover it. So we’re doing things to generate more revenue. Players will be seeing more of those because we’ve had them scheduled for a long time. We’re not the massive company behind Sims 4 (EA) and don’t make EA money, so all DLC sales are 100% “support-a-small-team-making-something-players-want-to-exist”. If this isn’t for you, absolutely no worries. More free stuff is coming soon via DLC, general content updates, and the Chemistry Update; we’re working on it.
[/p][p]Years ago I took a few months to create the tools necessary to make fish, plants, hardscape, and substrate, separating them from my workflow. Because of this, Erin and Josh can use these tools to make more content for the game without fear of interrupting whatever major update I’m working on. DLC updates don’t slow down free systems updates--they fund them. These DLC updates have been in the works since April 2024 after interacting with the community’s hopes for more fish. We release more free stuff like fish and substrate into the base game with each DLC and try to find ways to celebrate players through events like the seasonal hardscape.
[/p][p]All of this is to say that we care. We care about players’ experiences. We care about the fidelity of the game. We care about giving players content. We care about both new fishkeepers and the experienced ones. We care about finding the fun in the science and making that easy to play with. We’re really excited about this update and hope you are as well![/p][p]
[/p][p]-Ryan[/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: Small update to launch new DLC
notes.notes:
No major changes with this build, just a few small edits to the main menu to launch the new DLC!

-Ryan

notes.title: DLC and Fish Appearance Update!
notes.notes:
DLC
-Added Free Fish Pack and Asia Fish Pack #1
-Added menus, tutorials, etc. to support the new DLC feature
-Added a new store for DLC content that will help surface DLC items more frequently

Fish Appearance and Behavior
-HUGE audit to all fish textures, animations, and behaviors. Every fish should look/act better. Some fish look/act WAY better. Thank you Erin for combing through HUNDREDS of files by hand to make this possible.
-Updated and improved pectoral fin animations, which are now better connected to actual fish motion/intention
-Updated and improved Fish Iridescence
-Updated and improved Fish Transparency
-Updated and improved lighting on fish, who sometimes had harsh shadows on thin or transparent body parts
-Many quality of life improvements for the internal tools used to make Fish, resulting in better quality, faster production, and fewer headaches
-Updates to fish behavior, especially algae eating, territory guarding, and general movement
-Major improvement to fish schooling, removing "guppy death ball" scenario where an entire school would congregate in one location, oscillating up and down. Schools should now group together and move around as a unit, but not be so glued to each other.

Settings
-Added Resolution Scale setting to render the game window at a lower resolution as an optional way to improve performance
-Added setting to disable Surface Algae and poop. This was included to let players who use the -dx11 fix still play the game without everything covered in green

Misc
-Added warning to the Details Panel when someone is using No Death Mode
-Added functionality to Inspect tool that just zooms in on a point if clicking on hardscape or substrate
-Added names suggested by our Patreon supporters (thank you!)
-Added text to fish details that indicates what size it will grow to be (matching the suggestions when starting a new tank)
-Improved UI/menu animations
-New sounds, especially when interacting with UI buttons or in-tank items

Fixes
-Fixed bug that could erase keeper XP from the UI that had yet to be collected before traveling to a new tank/store
-Corrected typos
-Fixed back button in main menu
-Fixed Grab Highlight bug on fish
-Fixed examine mouseover not always showing the latest history event

notes.title: The JERK UPDATE
notes.notes:
Introducing the JERK UPDATE with a FREE NEW FISH whose behavior was designed with the help of YouTuber Drae!

Cichlid owners and aggro-fish curious folks REJOICE! IT’S TANK OF THRONES TIME. 

Before we get in to it: our discord's [url=https://t.co/IFOVmV4Omo]here[/url] if you want to join. You can have a real impact on the direction of the game. We're very close to 1000 members!

[b]OKAY[/b]

Just like people, some fish are [b]JERKS[/b]. For good or foul, it can’t be denied that jerks make their surroundings more... [i]interesting[/i]. 

[previewyoutube=CBqVqz8UfEY;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]Here’s what’s happening: 
[/b]

Fish (if it makes sense for the species) will regularly try to intimidate peers in the pecking order to elevate their own status or steal a territory. They’ll do this through a ton of improved and newly-added behaviors such as quiver & mouth-gape displays, lip-locking & flaring. 

[img]https://i.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExN240dHkzdzk2NmRmanh0aHc3NWI2OGV6NGhlOGtxb3BuODl0aHBvZiZlcD12MV9pbnRlcm5hbF9naWZfYnlfaWQmY3Q9Zw/p5k0REW3dFVTgdWI9n/giphy.gif[/img]

[img]https://i.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExNzZud3I0OGMyZXhqNGNib3dqaHc5YjJmdjVjcTU2ZWU0cjA4dW43eiZlcD12MV9pbnRlcm5hbF9naWZfYnlfaWQmY3Q9Zw/kpn9I2MTIKW8kBEjPU/giphy.gif[/img]

[img]https://i.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExaTd1djI4em93NnJhdG4zYWwzOHYzeDU2MThiaGo5cnJoeGVtdHQ3OSZlcD12MV9pbnRlcm5hbF9naWZfYnlfaWQmY3Q9Zw/VMnLrzycQtJGimsMtN/giphy.gif[/img]

Every fish has been updated to reflect their real-world counterparts, with a ton of improvements outside of the hierarchy system as well.

Depending on the result of the challenge, a fish’s hierarchy stat will increase or decrease, which affects its overall state of fear, which affects its overall health.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44655584/c25a4880e72225dc38690aadc452daac1624fb41.png[/img]

If the Tank Boss is weakened or another fish’s hierarchy stat increases enough, it becomes a target for rivals to challenge and boom, we’ve got a medieval grasp for the crown on our hands.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44655584/3e1451efc470b6933550b4cfb54c4034256e1dde.png[/img]

[b]Aquariums are now significantly more dynamic & interesting. Behaviour looks much more realistic, and the narratives developed in your aquariums are much higher stakes. 
[/b]

As a fishkeeper, this adds the challenge of building tanks that are the right size and decorated appropriately (breaking up lines of sight, providing lots of hiding spots) for everyone to get along. Or, you can do things “wrong”, see how they play out and learn more about species interactions without risking fish in real life–we’d rather it happen here!

To put the icing on the cake, we’ve added the rare & aggressive Atabapo Pike Cichlid–[url=https://www.youtube.com/@drae]YouTuber Drae[/url]’s favourite fish. We hopped on a call with him with Unreal open and he helped us make sure its behaviour was looking good!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44655584/34e798842a6899305b23f02e0f2c5d82b1f53bd8.png[/img]

[b]Here is the full change list (HUGE)! [/b]

[b]Improved Hierarchy System and Behaviors:
[/b]
-New Hierarchy system that influences aggression, coloration, swimming patterns, territory management, and chosen behaviors. Tank bosses emerge, are dethroned, and challenged by subordinates. Peace settles on tanks that have time to form stable communities. Moving a fish will make it forgive or forget, giving you the ability to actively balance or destabilize the system.  Dither fish and community size affect the chance that a fish will get targeted or harassed. Stability remains a moving target as fish age and new opportunities present themselves.
-Added Gape Display, Quiver Display, and Lip Lock Behaviors.
-Improved Guard Territory behavior to respect the improved hierarchy system. Fish can now be chased out of their territories or abandon them entirely if necessary.

[b]Improved Fish-Substrate interactions:
[/b]
-Added ability for fish to hold substrate in their mouths and spit it out in a different location.
-Added particle effects to fish swimming near the surface of the substrate.
-Added Sharpness to certain substrates, which will injure fish that spend time bumping into them.
-Improved audio for substrate scaping. The sound should now match the material being used.

[b]Added Community Scape Theme widget to the pause screen:
[/b]
-Updates every week with a new theme, with over 2 years' worth of themes to make and share with the community. 

[b]Improved Tutorial for better beginner experience:
[/b]
-Update to text, aiming to be less wordy and more to the point. 
-Short guided intro, to reduce the amount of random clicking with the goal "how do I get fish?"
-Added (?) buttons to all panels to make information more "opt in" and less forced.
-Added controls reminder for players who have never moved the camera after over an hour of play.
-Updated shop order to create a better flow for the first few hours of play.
-Rearranged Keeper XP items to make more sense for introducing players to content.

[b]Major UI polish improvements. There are dozens of changes and additions, but overall it should just feel nicer to interact with:
[/b]
-Added a basic sorting tool for the Fish Panel so you can order the fish by certain stats. This will likely be worked on for a little while longer, but this is a great start.
-Fixed UI bugs that created unreadable text or broken buttons when text was too long or the window was too small.
-Fixed Main Menu video playback, which had been laggy for reasons unrelated to game performance.
-Made most tools remember their state per tank, not per profile. This is better for a lot of situations, but the typical one is needing to select the right kind of food for a tank that has specific dietary needs. Now the last food you chose for that particular tank will be selected by the default. Less annoying clicking.
-Added pausing to the credits by clicking.
-Just so many animations and transitions. Probably more to come!

[b]Added new fish name system that is optionally localizable for languages that really should have a different name set:
[/b]-Added optional Species names, so fish species with extreme personalities can be given names that match them.

[b]Major behavior audit for all fish:
[/b]
-Many fish will have improved behaviors, making them more lifelike than before. This will apply to new fish; all your old ones will stay as they were.

[b]Misc Improvements:
[/b]
-Adjusted the color of algae that grows on glass and substrate. It had been acid green a little too long. It should now match the color of the algae in the water column.
-Improved the appearance of dust particles.
-Improved highlight effect on Fish, Plants and Hardscape so it is smoother and less jarring when switching between actors.
-Added highlight when the player hovers over an item in the Fish/Plant panel so it is easier to see the intended target. Prevents clicking many times while throwing the camera around looking for an individual. Also helps locate plants that are buried in a clump of other plants. Aquashella Daytona suggestion from one of the kids! Thank you!

[b]Bug Fixes:[/b]

-Fixed major bug with the game time/calendar that would freeze time after a large amount of play, which caused a large number of small seemingly unrelated errors.
-Fixed Ailment/Illness confusion with alerts. Fixed a number of bugs relating to alert icons.
-Fixed fish who like low water column regions warping under the substrate if it was thick enough to go above their max desired height. Fixed a similar issue with food being ignored when on thick substrate.
-Fixed fish getting "Illness" stat but no actual bacteria or parasites when eating other fish.
-Fixed Keeper XP bug that would fill the screen with a yellow circle sometimes.
-Fixed bug that would make eaten fish spawn into a bubble if clicked on via the Fish Panel.
-Fixed fish claiming territory outside the tank.
-Fixed plant and hardscape depth when squished against the tank glass, appearing between reflecting parts, not just inside the tank. 
-Fixed sorting problem with leaves when pressed against the glass. They no longer clip through each other. 
-Fixed Hornwort text, which had been duplicated from Cabomba plant text.
-Fixed certain settings not being initialized properly when spawning. (Framerate and VSYNC)
-Added setting for turning off substrate damage.
-Added setting for turning off toilet joke when deleting fish.

notes.title: Plant Bug Fixes
notes.notes:
Thanks to our Superfins beta testers (this and more on the Discord! https://discord.gg/qrHdQnFk ), I was able to corner and smoosh a whole bunch of plant related bugs this week. Sorry to anyone who might have had disappearing plants! You can get them to reappear by clicking on them in the Plant Panel; they will reappear in a bubble, so you can put them back where they belong. Thanks for playing. We appreciate you!

-Ryan, the one who makes the bugs

[list]
[*] Fixed bug the prevented hardscape from being placed high enough in short tanks.
[*] Fixed bug that broke plant loading for plants with a period in their names (Made them disappear when trying to add to the inventory)
[*] Fixed floaters not being spawned into stores.
[*] Fixed some plants from being spawned with broken rotations.
[*] Added way for phantom plants/fish to be spawned back into the tank so they can be managed. (Clicking on them in the panel spawns an identity bubble)
[*] Fixed store spawning problems that were sending plants, hardscape, and fish to the very bottom of the tank almost always.
[*] Reorganized the way the substrate and water both animate in to prevent situations where the height is lower than it should be based on an animation state.
[*] Added a last ditch fix to plants that spawn in with no components, which would make them completely invisible and ungrowable. If this happens they should hard reboot, creating a newish plant in the same location.
[/list]

notes.title: SUBSTRATE UPDATE & LIMITED-TIME HARDSCAPE!
notes.notes:
Hello everyone! Just in time for the Steam Summer Sale we're introducing a [b]major update to substrates[/b] and a pile of [b]LIMITED TIME SUMMER ASSETS[/b]. 

We've added a pile of new substrates including several different kinds of gravel, aquarium soil, coated gravel, and glass beads. And if you thought we couldn't make a ridiculous trailer about dirt & rocks, you thought wrong. I'd say how many we're adding, but I am writing this a couple days in advance and there might be a couple more that'll make their way in before the update goes live. At least 19. 

[previewyoutube=OW6xU5Qs52Y;full][/previewyoutube]

Not only are new substrates available, but you can have as many different substrates in a tank as you like and layer them on top of one another. Create sand art, differentiate biomes; tons of possibilities!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44655584/b22deffcd4d6907542801f055090e9b8ca51311b.png[/img]

[b]COMING SOON[/b]: non-inert substrates will have significant interplay with water chemistry. 

Along with this update, and for a LIMITED TIME ONLY, we've got a pile of summer hardscape. Skulls with sunglasses (why not), shells, beach balls & more. [b]These will only be available during the summer sale[/b], but once you have them, you've got'em forever!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44655584/dccffa921a59994b79268410d23ee581f59d611d.png[/img]

We can't wait to see your new tanks!!!

Our game is a labor of love & a passion project. Please tell your friends, join our [url=https://t.co/IFOVmV5mbW]discord[/url], wishlist and stay tuned for more!

Other changes: 

[b]Updated features:
[/b][list]
[*] Option in the game settings added to allow for flat fish.
[*] Hardscape exact dimensions are now in the hardscape tooltip.
[*] Tooltips for the game clock now reflects how much time a player has played in game-days and game-years.
[*] Water volume is now tracked in connection to the amount of substrate in a tank, which impacts the amount of swim space a fish senses.
[*] Fun new font!
[*] Custom tanks can now go down to 1 gallon (you monster).
[/list]

[b]Alerts update:
[/b][list]
[*] The alert system has been streamlined to make player notifications easier to navigate.
[*] Players can now see an alert indicator in the tank panel, fish panel, and plant panel as needs arise.
[*] Panel icons now have an indicator number for the alerts within that panel.
[/list]

[b]Bug fixes:
[/b][list]
[*] Rapid fish vibration has been eliminated.
[*] Food is now affected by time controls.
[*] Hardscape will no longer be lost below the tank and will be moved into the inventory when released in an odd space in the tank.
[*] Fish will no longer appear flattened on the tank glass, but an option to retain that bug is in the settings menu for players who liked it.
[*] Fish will no longer present with shortened spines that had created oddly short, stubby fish.
[*] Improved tanks' visual spawning.
[*] Plants and fish located in an inventory bubble at the top of a tank are no longer lost and remain in those bubbles upon returning to a tank.
[*] Plants and fish don't die in inventory bubbles.
[*] Gaps between the substrate and glass have been eliminated, meaning fish and food will no longer get stuck there.
[*] All player-facing fish size data now agrees.
[/list]

notes.title: Bug fix update 4.24.2024
notes.notes:
Addressed inventory bug and medicine stress permanent status. 

--Items should no longer disappear/reappear at random.
--Stress from medicine should resolve as intended after water changes instead of permanently affecting fish.

notes.title: Adorable Abominations Update
notes.notes:
Hello Fish Gamers!

While we work on the next major systems update, we’ve got a very exciting and highly-requested content update for you, dubbed the Adorable Abominations Update. FANCY GOLDFISH and MORE! [b]Our biggest content update since launch![/b]

As per usual, I’ve amused myself by making an update-specific trailer: 
[previewyoutube=6vH987dx3gc;full][/previewyoutube]

What does this delightful dump of genetic tinkering include? 

Introducing:
[list]
[*] [b]Ranchu Goldfish[/b] - 7 varieties
[*] [b]Ryukin Goldfish[/b] - 4 varieties
[*] [b]Shubunkin Goldfish[/b] - 6 varieties
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44655584/6c1b6dc5046d9c4f04919dcb42e41b6cbb5a4ab4.jpg[/img]

And we’ve also added [b]5 varieties[/b] of the glorious carp that started it all: [b]KOI[/b]! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44655584/95e96e5b82dc14c06df546564c7be3b7053b2ec6.jpg[/img]

And 3 new varieties of common goldfish. 25 new varieties of fish in all!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44655584/678f82a953756135fc32a1b3c7a6d2e7726d3156.png[/img]

Fish game now has 134 varieties of fish to choose from! That’s a lot of fish! Double that once you factor in both sexes!

We couldn’t do this without your support. Please tell your fish friends about the game so we can continue to add more content. You can also help by reviewing us on Steam if you like the game. [url=https://t.co/IFOVmV5mbW]Join our discord[/url] to chat with us and have a real influence on the direction of the game. This update was completely inspired by community input.

More soon!

Swimmily,

Gord & the Fish Game Team

notes.title: "Get Ich & Die" Update + Steepest Discount Since Launch!
notes.notes:
Hello Fish Gamers! Big update this month. A lot of these improvements were from discord suggestions, so if you haven’t already be sure to join by clicking the button on the bottom left. 

First up! One many players have been looking forward to but the fish certainly have not: 

[b]DISEASE[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44655584/0296a3497c3a1526707296545f3e52e8af2e8acd.png[/img]

We consulted with the lovely scientists & experts at the [url=https://gettingfishypod.substack.com/]Gettin’ Fishy With it Pod[/url] on which diseases we should include and how they should be treated and spread. We have 6 gross ailments spread across 2 categories:

[b]Bacteria[/b]
[list]
[*] Body Fungus
[*] Fin Rot
[*] Popeye
[/list]
[b]Parasite[/b]
[list]
[*] Velvet
[*] Hole in Head disease
[*] Ich
[/list]
For those more into [i]escaping[/i] the disgusting realities of fishkeeping, you will be able to toggle both the visual nastiness or diseases as a whole in the options.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44655584/e8f44f0ce17a934814f40fbf3aa75d26f8bcae39.png[/img]

[b]But, good news[/b], we’ve also added medicine for each of these afflictions. Standard recommended treatments of reducing stress and using hospital tanks is of course also vital!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44655584/858a92cc417c2f947edd32451171903dae88fa2f.png[/img]

[b]Other great stuff![/b]

[list]
[*] [b]Cloud Saves![/b] They work now. And save files will be smaller. Hop between machines or between your steam deck and PC.
[*] [b]Fish love you back.[/b] Fish will recognize when you’ve come back to see them and say hi. Naturally skittish fish will hide, and they will warm up to you over time if you take good care of them.
[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExMnJqMzV6bTZ6NnFtcjBuMTAxNzdhZmpyMHhseHowanZzb2oxdmNlZyZlcD12MV9pbnRlcm5hbF9naWZfYnlfaWQmY3Q9Zw/8z0D5r0TVkEioXBxNj/giphy.gif[/img]
[*] [b]Varied fish & plant max growths[/b] for a more natural and realistic experience. 
[*] [b]Plants are now rotatable[/b] for even more detailed scaping!
[*] [b]Plant root needs now matter![/b] For instance: rhizome plants will not survive in substrate.
[*] [b]We’ve improved the appearance and UI/UX of the shops for easier use[/b]; no more (or at least less!) bonkers floating hardscape, and some of them–while still procedurally generated–might even look pretty darn nice and inspire some scapin’ ideas.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44655584/1fa9f77ea0fab2b820de3ee98bcebf0415fbdac3.png[/img] 
[*] [b]New music![/b] New tunes from A Shell in the Pit. Also some updated sounds and audio fixes.
[*] [b]Improved UI scaling for Steam Deck[/b], and updated controls. We should be ready to upgrade our sad “playable” to “verified” shortly. 
[*] [b]Player cursor variable speed option[/b] added to settings. A discord request!
[*] [b]Smoother tank transitions[/b]
[*] [b]Improved Alerts[/b] so they are less chaotic and more reliable.
[*] [b]Fish Respawn[/b] only in places they’ve been to recently, so they should no longer appear in random locations. You can finally build your two sided tanks with a mountain in the middle!
[*] [b]Fixed Revenge Death Spirals[/b] and lowered the amount of injury sustained from nipping. If one aggressive fish bit a second aggressive fish they would immediately trigger a “revenge” attack which would trigger another attack (etc) until someone died…very quickly. Revenge should only happen once now.
[*] [b]Many other bug fixes and improvements[/b] including Chemistries loading correctly, dragging hardscape out from the inventory without vanishing issues, fixed fish ages not tracking while the player was not present, fixed plants attached to hardscape getting lost when moving hardscape to the inventory, fixed fish bouncing on the top of the water, improved world lighting to reduce harsh shadows, and improved polish on some UI elements/buttons.
[/list]

notes.title: UPDATE: FEMALE FISH - SEPARATE BREEDING UPDATE IS PLANNED FOR DOWN THE ROAD
notes.notes:
Hello everyone! We are thr-gilled to announce that in time for Valentine’s Day, we are welcoming female fish to the game! You can expect to start finding male and female fish in shops with this update. We can’t get too romantic, however, as the breeding update will be a while. 

https://youtu.be/RfITvIkz1Ms

For some of the species, female fish will be visibly different from the male counterparts, either in size, color, or model. For other species, even scientists can’t seem to find a difference, so females will look the same.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44655584/38d532534e0a08dce1d435390b4e3e0d8b0e019b.png[/img]

Keep an eye out for new behaviors that these gal pals will introduce. We don’t want to spoil anything, but–love them or hate them–betta sororities are now a possibility!

And some more exciting news: the bridle shiner will be making its debut in this update! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44655584/d9303da8fcb2f9a1c037e43c0e3f488f7875d0b2.png[/img]

The bridle shiner is a species of special concern for one of our favorite YouTubers, [url=https://www.youtube.com/@AVNJ]AVNJ[/url], who even helped us design the behavior! You can watch that in action [url=https://m.twitch.tv/videos/2058153616]here[/url]. We’re hoping its inclusion will bring awareness to an at-risk fish species.

That’s all for now, but we’re deep into work for the next update already. In the meantime, we’re looking forward to seeing your Valentine’s date night tanks!

If you want to talk to us or share and chat with the community, come on over to our discord.

notes.title: UPDATE NOV 28 2023 - Better Lighting & Bye Bye to VRAM Crashes.
notes.notes:
Hello all! We've got a nice update here for you. Increased stability, more bugs squashed (except the fish squashing bug... people seem to be enjoying that one). 

[b]ADDED[/b] - Faked Global Illumination. Light should now appear to bounce off the substrate, subtly providing an under-lit effect depending on the color of the substrate and brightness of the light. In short, tanks should look prettier and more realistically lit. Big thanks to Mark Laprairie (Hot Lava Creator) on the suggestion and how to approach this!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44655584/0ff580a84a37b835ec298589034016edd86962ae.png[/img]

[b]ADDED [/b]- Option to control bubble aquantity. They do represent game chemistry, but they're not making everyone feel, ahem, [i]bubbly[/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44655584/216e54cce675560354a730cc3055e2cb9cb9b1b3.png[/img]

[b]ADDED [/b]- Option to disable auto-zoom when examining fish.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44655584/82cff5ceabbce93d0ef31b7fc2d6ed44658da6ff.png[/img]

[b]ADDED [/b]- Purple Sand substrate option because someone asked for it during our fishwiki stream and it took 2 seconds to add. Ooooh! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44655584/98730c65426945b692b67566802a771586d55eda.png[/img]

[b]CHANGED [/b]- Floating plants now always have full 02 and CO2, since they are in contact with the air.
[b]CHANGED [/b]- Camera Zoom should be easier to navigate larger tanks, particularly at the edges.

[b]FIXED [/b]- [b]BIG ONE![/b] Greatly improved Texture Memory (VRAM) throughout the game. This should fix a bug that prevented some players from opening their game after several hours of play, allow lower-end graphics cards to play the game, and allow the game to use better textures for all players who are opting to have more crowded tanks.
[b]FIXED [/b]- [b]BIG ONE![/b] Plants duplicating themselves on load. No more out of control "growth". Plants should also load in their correct positions as a result!
[b]FIXED [/b]- Bug that slowly lowered tank light over time.
[b]FIXED [/b]- ZOMBIE FISH. Fish could revive after dying, even after being eaten.
[b]FIXED [/b]- Glass Backgrounds duplicating.
[b]FIXED [/b]- Typos throughout the game.

We're still in post-launch cleanup mode, but will have bigger & more exciting updates for you soon!

Reminder: Join our Discord! https://t.co/IFOVmV5mbW

notes.title: Launch Update and Discord Invite Link!
notes.notes:
Hi everyone! 

[b]Launch Update[/b]: We wanted to release tomorrow but XBox just announced they’re doing a showcase and our PR team said it’d be a bad idea.

Anyway, even if something else crazy happens, we won’t be releasing outside of this week. The game MUST be out before the weekend for an even bigger marketing reason. As for the game, it’s ready to go; I’m literally hovering over the button waiting for people to tell me we can go live. Sorry for the delays; I know it's annoying for you dedicated wonderful few, but in order to give the game its best chance to become a thing that lasts a long time we need as many eyes on it as possible. 

[b]Discord[/b]: We have a [url=https://discord.gg/EWkmMecD]discord[/url] now! <--This invite link is good for 7 days. Please feel free to join if that’s your jam to chat with fellow virtual tankbuilders, share tanks, feedback on the game, and maybe even take part in a contest or two. Please make sure you read the community guidelines, and note that dev response time will be regular but not immediate as we’ve got busy lives and this game to make, and no allocated budget for a community manager or anything at the moment. All our money right now is going into building the best game we can & getting it in people’s faces. 

Discord not your thing? Head on over to our subreddit! [url=https://www.reddit.com/r/fishgame]/r/fishgame[/url]

Cheers!

G

notes.title: RELEASE DELAYED :(
notes.notes:
Hi Everyone, Gord (creator) here. 

Real sorry about this! No one is more disappointed than me, believe me--I pulled an all-nighter finishing the Announce Date trailer. 

The good news is that we're not delaying because the game's not ready, it's ready and we are unbelievably proud of it. 

We are just waiting on build approval from Steam and that's a 2-5 business day process. Long story short: I thought we submitted it alongside the demo build and noticed on Weds I [i]most certainly [/i] had not. No one to blame but myself--not getting a lot of sleep these days and the stupid mistakes are rolling in.

We believe we could be approved as early as Monday, or as late as Wednesday. If you have a press key, you should be able to play as early as Saturday afternoon (PST). Will update here, on twitter ([url=https://twitter.com/afishgame]@afishgame[/url]) and on our subreddit ([url=https://www.reddit.com/r/fishgame/]r/fishgame[/url]). We'll have a discord up & running next week as well!

Thanks for your patience! We're really looking forward to seeing your tanks, hearing your fishy stories, and soaking up your feedback. 

Fish on,

Gord
